newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLAND BEAT SOUTH AFRICA IN UNINSPIRING FRIENDLY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND BEAT SOUTH AFRICA IN UNINSPIRING FRIENDLY.

text.p: Goals by Robert Lee and Ian Wright gave England a 2-1 win over South Africa in a scrappy first international between the two countries at Old Trafford on Saturday.

England manager Glenn Hoddle made eight changes from the side that beat Georgia in a World Cup qualifier last month and the team that meets Poland in another qualifier next Saturday is unlikely to bear much relation to the side that played in this match.
England went ahead after 20 minutes when Lee fired home at the second attempt for his second goal for his country in his 10th international.

The African champions flattered to decieve for much of the match with some fancy footwork in midfield. But they stunned England with a 43rd minute equaliser from Philemon Masinga, once of Leeds United, who headed home on the line after being set up by an overhead kick from John Moshoeu.

England clinched the victory which they just about deserved when Ian Wright scored after 75 minutes when he slid the ball in from close range after Paul Scholes nodded on a Paul Gascoigne freekick. TV replays showed the ball hit Wright's hand before he scored.

Midfielder Paul Gascoigne was carried off in the last minute with an ice-pack on his right leg after a reckless challenge by substitute Linda Buthelezi. Gascoigne was reported to have suffered a calf injury.
